answer.evidence: The column scan at x=8 shows one tan row at row 0, then a slightly lighter brown at rows 1-3, then flat dark brown down to row 14. There is no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so the post has at most a 1-row rim and no top surface. The sheet band at x=0-3 is a vertical strip of alternating teal and rust tiles in rows 0-15. It has no top plane or edge line, and it is drawn as a flat plan or elevation pattern rather than a 3/4 volume. There is no base or beam top face. The opaque silhouette is 11 px wide in rows 0-13, and the checkered area to the right lies outside it. The object therefore reads as a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical strip with a dark wood post and a band of overlapping corrugated sheet tops. It is small at 2x, so detail is hard to read by eye, and I lean on the measured facts. It shows 16 visible tones per full tile, which is level with the stall (17) and close to the well (20), and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark brown beside wood and sheet) rather than a black sticker line. By eye the sheet band shows alternating light and dark corrugation ridges plus a wood grain ramp on the post, about 4 steps per material against roughly 5 for the references. It is a little shallower than the best references, but it is not sticker-like and it is not thinner than the bench or lamp props. A careful artist would accept it next to them.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow vertical piece with a wood post on one side and a band of overlapping corrugated sheet tops on the other. It is thin, so I judged it by eye as well as by the numbers. Measured facts: 16 visible tones per tile, above the hedge (9) and close to the stall (17) and well (20).
